name: Due
description: Due is a reminder and timer app for iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Mac that emphasizes fast natural-language entry, reusable timers, persistent auto-snooze alerts, and optional iCloud or Dropbox synchronization.
agentUseSummary: Due cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because its documented URL scheme and Siri Shortcuts execute through an installed Apple-platform app, while reminders and timers remain on the user's devices or personal iCloud or Dropbox and Due publishes no server-side account API.

blocked.label: Connect Due
blocked.description: Relay does not present Apple, iCloud, Dropbox, Setapp, subscription, or installed-app state as a Railway API connection and does not silently substitute a device-local authority.

blocked.label: Use Due automation
blocked.description: Due's URL and callback scheme, Siri Shortcuts, Alfred and LaunchBar workflows, and local export require an installed app and device state that Relay cannot currently mount.

blocked.label: Access Due data
blocked.description: Relay does not request Apple or Dropbox credentials, inspect local Due databases or exported JSON, reuse app state, automate app UI, or call private synchronization services.

blocked.label: Change reminders or timers
blocked.description: Searching, reading, creating, editing, completing, snoozing, rescheduling, synchronizing, exporting, or deleting reminders and timers remains unavailable until Relay ships explicit local execution and approval boundaries.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized device-local Due connector using supported automation.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to Due, its URL scheme, Siri Shortcuts, local databases, or private iCloud and Dropbox synchronization.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to Due, its URL scheme, Siri Shortcuts, local databases, or private iCloud and Dropbox synchronization.

providerSetup.blocker: Due publishes a local URL and callback scheme for opening its add-reminder and search interfaces plus Siri Shortcuts, but no authorized third-party cloud account API. Due states that user-created reminders and timers are stored locally, are never transmitted to Due's servers, and optionally synchronize through the user's personal iCloud or Dropbox account. Relay's current Marketplace runtime intentionally excludes local-app command execution and cannot truthfully expose that authority from Railway.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Apple, iCloud, Dropbox, Setapp, subscription, or app credentials; inspect local databases or exports; automate Due; call private sync services; or show Connect. Reconsider after Relay ships a separately disclosed Apple-device local-connection architecture with app presence, pinned reviewed operations, per-action approval, result redaction, audit, and no cloud fallback, or Due supplies a current distributable server-side API contract.

evidence.supports: Due documents an app-local URL and x-callback scheme whose add action launches a prefilled reminder interface and whose search action opens Due to matching local reminders.
Due documents Siri Shortcuts on Apple devices for creating reminders, including repeating reminders, through the installed app.
Due states that reminders and timers are stored locally and never transmitted to or stored on Due servers, with optional synchronization through the user's personal iCloud or Dropbox account.
Due documents user-configured app synchronization through iCloud or Dropbox, merge and replace decisions, and an installed-app requirement for changes and alerts to take effect on iOS.
Due documents local database and JSON export access from the Mac file system rather than a provider-hosted data API.
